mechanism: VELGRAFT is a living allogeneic cellular skin substitute applied topically to diabetic foot ulcers. It contains human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells and MSC-derived adipocytes on a porous chitosan-gelatin matrix, intended to provide a temporary extracellular scaffold plus cellular paracrine signals that support host-cell migration, angiogenesis, tissue remodeling, and wound closure.
development_status: Recruiting U.S. Phase 1 randomized, double-blind, active-controlled study in up to 24 patients with chronic diabetic foot ulcers that have attained granulation tissue. ClinicalTrials.gov lists actual start on 2026-03-11, estimated primary completion and study completion on 2026-10-13, no expanded access, FDA-regulated drug product status, and no posted results.
clinical_summary: VELGRAFT is differentiated mechanistically from passive moist dressings because it combines a biodegradable chitosan-gelatin scaffold with living MSCs and adipocyte-differentiated MSCs. Ayu describes use in chronic non-infected wounds including diabetic foot ulcers, and a goat excision-wound study reported enhanced wound closure, collagen deposition, re-epithelialization, hair follicle formation, and angiogenesis-marker expression. However, the assigned human DFU study is small Phase 1, has no posted results, and competes in a managed class that already includes FDA-approved cellular skin substitutes such as Apligraf and Dermagraft.
safety_summary: No human VELGRAFT safety results are posted. The active study defines dose-limiting toxicities within 7 days as grade 3 or higher hypersensitivity, grade 3 or higher rash, grade 2 or higher skin infection, or death not clearly unrelated to treatment. Ayu's product page contraindicates use in infected wounds, severely immunocompromised patients, wounds exposing muscle/tendon/bone/joint capsule, or severe allergic reaction during patch testing; it also emphasizes single use, cold-chain storage, living-cell handling, and avoidance of cytotoxic wound-cleansing solutions.
management_tools: Treat as investigational/non-covered until U.S. approval and coding status are clear
Medical benefit prior authorization if launched
Require chronic non-infected DFU documentation, standard wound-care failure, adequate perfusion, debridement, offloading, and no exposed tendon, muscle, capsule, or bone
Require wound measurements and photographic documentation with ruler before and during treatment
Limit units to wound surface area and available product sizes; require documentation of wastage
Limit number of applications per wound episode and require measurable improvement for continuation
Site-of-care and cold-chain handling controls for living-cell product storage and application
evidence_gaps: No posted human efficacy or safety results for VELGRAFT in diabetic foot ulcers.
No disclosed U.S. regulatory pathway, approved indication, HCPCS code, reimbursement category, or commercial price for VELGRAFT.

ClinicalTrials.gov lists the trial as studying an FDA-regulated drug product and not an FDA-regulated device product, while Ayu describes VELGRAFT as a combination product with biologic and device constituents.
Ayu's public product page appears to promote VELGRAFT for multiple wound types and shows CE-mark imagery, but this does not establish U.S. FDA approval for diabetic foot ulcers.
Cost estimate is analog-derived from 2026 CMS skin-substitute payment context and VELGRAFT listed sizes, not VELGRAFT acquisition price.

sources.title: Phase 1 Study of VELGRAFT, a Living Cellular Construct, in the Management of Chronic Diabetic Foot Ulcers Which Have Attained Granulation Tissue
supports: Sponsor is Ayu, Inc.; collaborator is MCRA.
VELGRAFT intervention is an allogeneic cell-based product containing living human bone marrow-derived MSCs and MSCs differentiated into adipocytes on a porous chitosan-gelatin matrix.
Trial is recruiting, Phase 1, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, and estimated to enroll 24 patients.
Actual start date is 2026-03-11; estimated primary completion and study completion are 2026-10-13.
Part A escalates from one to four weekly VELGRAFT applications to identify maximum tolerated application; Part B randomizes patients 1:1 to VELGRAFT or standard moist dressing.

Primary outcome is treatment-emergent adverse events; secondary outcomes include complete wound closure, percent area reduction, time to wound closure, closure rate, recurrence, re-epithelialization, scar assessment, and quality of life.
The study has no posted results and lists FDA-regulated drug product status.

sources.title: VELGRAFT - Allogenic Cellular Skin Substitute for Advanced Wound Care by AYU Lifescience
supports: Ayu describes VELGRAFT as an allogeneic cellular skin substitute for non-infected wounds, consisting of a polymeric scaffold seeded with hMSCs and stem-cell-derived adipocytes.
Company mechanism claims include temporary extracellular scaffold function, host-cell migration support, growth factors and cytokines released by embedded hMSCs, angiogenesis, and tissue remodeling.
Listed intended wound types include diabetic foot ulcers, burns, venous leg ulcers, and other suitable partial- or full-thickness wounds.
Listed sizes include circular 9.5 cm2, 21 cm2, 55 cm2, and 100 cm2 products and a rectangular 144 cm2 product.
Product attributes include aseptic processing, 25-day shelf life, 4-8 degrees C storage, single use, and precautions for a living-cell product.
Contraindications include infected wound site, severe immunocompromise, exposed muscle/tendon/bone/joint capsule, and severe allergic reaction during patch testing.

sources.title: Chitosan and gelatin biopolymer supplemented with mesenchymal stem cells (Velgraft) enhanced wound healing in goats (Capra hircus): Involvement of VEGF, TGF and CD31
supports: Preclinical goat excision-wound study evaluated Velgraft, a chitosan and gelatin biopolymer supplemented with MSCs and MSCs differentiated into adipocytes.
Velgraft-treated wounds showed improved wound closure by day 21, restoration of skin architecture, collagen fibers, blood capillaries, and hair follicular formation.
Study reported stimulation of CD31, VEGF, and TGF-beta1 expression after Velgraft application.
The paper disclosed Datt Mediproducts Pvt. Ltd. provided the test subject and financial assistance.

sources.title: Premarket Approval P950032/S016: APLIGRAF (GRAFTSKIN)
supports: FDA PMA supplement approved Apligraf for use with standard diabetic foot ulcer care.

Approved DFU population includes full-thickness neuropathic diabetic foot ulcers of greater than three weeks duration that have not adequately responded to conventional therapy and extend through the dermis without tendon, muscle, capsule, or bone exposure.
Apligraf is an FDA-approved cellular skin-substitute analog for DFU clinical and coverage context.

sources.title: Apligraf Fact Sheet and Essential Prescribing Information
supports: Apligraf is a living bi-layered skin substitute manufactured from neonatal foreskin-derived keratinocytes and fibroblasts with bovine Type I collagen.

Apligraf is indicated with standard diabetic foot ulcer care for full-thickness neuropathic foot ulcers of at least three weeks duration that have not adequately responded to conventional therapy and lack tendon, muscle, capsule, or bone exposure.
Contraindications include clinically infected wounds and allergies to bovine collagen or agarose shipping medium.
DFU patients should receive Apligraf with good ulcer care including non-weight-bearing regimen, optimal metabolic control, and nutrition.

sources.title: Calendar Year 2026 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule Final Rule - Skin Substitutes
supports: CMS stated Medicare Part B spending for skin substitutes rose from $252 million in 2019 to more than $10 billion in 2024.
For CY 2026, CMS finalized payment for skin substitute products as incident-to supplies when used as part of covered application procedures in non-facility and hospital outpatient settings.
CMS aligned skin substitute categorization with FDA regulatory status, including 361 HCT/Ps, PMAs, and 510(k)s.
CMS finalized a single CY 2026 payment rate of approximately $127.28 for skin substitute products across the categories as an initial policy.

sources.title: Skin and Soft Tissue Substitutes - Medical Clinical Policy Bulletin 0244
supports: Aetna coverage criteria for Apligraf, Dermagraft, Grafix, EpiFix, and other skin substitutes include chronic DFU use with standard diabetic ulcer care and no exposed tendon, muscle, capsule, or bone.
Continuation criteria limit chronic wound treatment to no more than 12 weeks and generally no more than 10 applications per 12-week period.
Aetna requires photographic documentation with ruler and evidence that the wound is improving.
Aetna considers continued treatment not medically necessary if the ulcer fails to heal by at least 50% within the first 6 weeks or if treatment extends beyond 12 weeks.

expected_launch_window.method: Derived from first U.S. Phase 1 recruiting status, estimated study completion in October 2026, absence of human results, and likely need for larger controlled DFU efficacy and safety evidence plus regulatory review before launch.
expected_launch_window.explanation: The current study can establish early safety and dose/application frequency, but a U.S. launch before 2030 is unlikely without additional pivotal evidence and clarity on the biologic-device combination regulatory route.

annual_cost_range.method: Used CMS CY 2026 skin-substitute payment analog of $127.28 per cm2. Low case assumes one smallest listed VELGRAFT size: 9.5 cm2 x $127.28 = $1,209. High case assumes four applications using the listed 21 cm2 product size to cover an ulcer near the trial's 20 cm2 maximum: 21 cm2 x 4 x $127.28 = $10,692.
annual_cost_range.explanation: VELGRAFT is investigational and unpriced; estimate reflects analog product payment context for one annual DFU wound episode and excludes application procedures, debridement, offloading, visits, infection management, wastage policy, rebates, and any future premium pricing for living-cell handling.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted VELGRAFT's living MSC/adipocyte chitosan-gelatin construct and preclinical wound-healing evidence against lack of posted human DFU results and the existence of FDA-approved cellular skin-substitute analogs.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: The mechanism is biologically differentiated from passive dressings and aligns with regenerative wound-care approaches, but current human evidence is too early to support a stronger differentiation rating.

budget_impact.method: Assessed from potentially broad DFU population, high Medicare skin-substitute spending growth, multi-application wound episodes, and availability of standard medical-benefit utilization controls.
budget_impact.explanation: Per-episode analog cost is material but manageable with wound-size, application-count, and continuation controls; population-level exposure could be meaningful if VELGRAFT is broadly adopted in chronic DFU care.

disruption_risk.method: Balanced early Phase 1 stage and no human results against a living-cell product profile, cold-chain/site handling needs, possible coding/reimbursement complexity, and a large, scrutinized skin-substitute spend category.
disruption_risk.explanation: Near-term clinical disruption is limited, but launch could require payer policy updates, wound-center controls, and episode-level documentation rules if efficacy is demonstrated.

recommended_action.method: Mapped early Phase 1 recruiting status, no posted results, no price, and unclear U.S. coding/regulatory route to monitoring with payer-preparation triggers.
recommended_action.explanation: Track Phase 1 safety/application findings, subsequent pivotal-trial plans, FDA regulatory pathway, HCPCS/payment status, and any U.S. launch or coding announcements before building active coverage policy.
